business_scope.primary_industry_name: Interactive Audio Chatroom and Companion Social Applications

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Quebec (Province of Canada), with commercial seat in Montreal; registry: Registraire d'entreprise du Québec (REQ)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Civil Law under the Civil Code of Quebec (CQLR c CCQ-1991) for private and commercial matters; Common Law for federal public law, criminal law, and federal tax administration; bilingual French/English legal proceedings
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA/USMCA), in force 1 July 2020
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), in force 30 December 2018 for Canada
Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), provisionally in force since 21 September 2017
Agreement between Canada and the People's Republic of China for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments, in force 1 October 2014
Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement, in force 1 April 2021
Over 90 bilateral income tax conventions (DTAAs) currently in force, including the Canada-United States Tax Convention (1980, as amended by the 2007 Protocol)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended, together with the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184, and the Suspicious Transaction Reporting Regulations, SOR/2002-317; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, ss. 83.01 et seq. and 462.3 et seq.; United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2; Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; Quebec Legal Publicity Act, CQLR c P-44.1, and Regulation respecting the register of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, r. 1; Civil Code of Quebec, CQLR c CCQ-1991, arts. 2209-2253 (société en commandite); Quebec Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11; federal Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, s. 21.1 (individuals with significant control register, used as the national UBO benchmark). The mandatory identification threshold for beneficial owners is 25% or more of the partnership interests or control rights, direct or indirect.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of corporate existence or registry extract for each corporate partner (including the corporate general partner) evidencing good standing and authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the partner's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the 1961 Hague Convention (in force for Canada since 11 January 2024); for non-Convention states, consular legalization through Global Affairs Canada and the relevant embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing the Quebec formation agent and law firm to register the limited partnership and execute statutory filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary in the principal's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, accompanied by a certified French/English translation by a Quebec-certified translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copies and current proof of residential address for each ultimate beneficial owner and limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority and a utility provider or regulated financial institution in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for notarized copies where required; original passports and original proof-of-address documents may alternatively be presented physically to the Quebec formation agent under FINTRAC identification rules

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming the lawful source of funds for the proposed initial capital contribution of each limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Account-holding bank of the contributing partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature with Hague Apostille or consular legalization if the letter must be relied upon outside the issuing bank's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory at onboarding: (1) FINTRAC-compliant identification and verification of all partners and any individual exercising control of or owning 25% or more of the partnership; (2) determination of foreign PEP, domestic PEP, head of an international organization, family member, or close associate status for every identified person; (3) enhanced due diligence and written senior-management approval before onboarding any foreign PEP; (4) screening against the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, the Criminal Code s. 83.05 terrorist entity list, Canadian regulations under the Special Economic Measures Act (including measures against Russia, Belarus, Iran, Syria, Venezuela, and Haiti) and the United Nations Act, and, as prudent market practice, the US OFAC SDN list and UK HMT consolidated sanctions list; (5) adverse-media and negative-news searches on each UBO; (6) documented source-of-funds declaration for the initial contribution given the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML tier applicable to ISIC 6311 voice streaming social applications; and (7) annual re-screening and continuous transaction monitoring, with all results timestamped and retained in the AML/KYC file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire d'entreprise du Québec (REQ) - Registre des entreprises en ligne, official portal: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca (integrated name search and preliminary name clearance service)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11, every business name registered in Quebec must be in French or include a French version with the French text prevalent ('caractère prépondérant') in all commercial signage and documentation. The statutory legal designator for a limited partnership must appear as 'société en commandite' or the abbreviation 'S.E.C.'. Non-French names require transliteration into Latin characters accepted by the REQ; the transliteration must preserve the phonetic and visual distinctiveness of the name in French to avoid confusion with existing registrants in the provincial registry.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Tokens requiring prior ministerial, professional-order, or regulatory authorization: 'Banque'/'Bank', 'Fiducie'/'Trust', 'Assurance'/'Insurance', 'Titres'/'Securities', 'Finance', 'Université'/'University', 'Collège'/'College', 'Commission', 'Municipalité', 'Régie', 'Office', 'Ministère'/'Ministry', 'Gouvernement'/'Government', 'Société de la Couronne'/'Crown Corporation', 'Royal'/'Royale', 'Police', 'Gendarmerie', 'Parti politique'

Reserved professional titles the misuse of which constitutes a penal offence: 'Avocat'/'Lawyer', 'Notaire'/'Notary', 'Comptable professionnel agréé'/'CPA', 'Médecin'/'Physician', 'Dentiste', 'Pharmacien', 'Ingénieur'/'Engineer', 'Architecte', 'Ordre professionnel'
Obscene, scandalous, misleading, or hateful expressions; names that suggest public authority or a government connection; and names likely to incite ethnic, religious, or social hatred

Names that phonetically or visually reproduce a name already registered at the REQ, a distinctive element of an existing enterprise, or a trademark protected under the Trademarks Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. T-13
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon receiving a written REQ refusal stating the statutory grounds (confusion, non-compliance with the French-language regime, or public-order objections), the applicant shall: (1) prepare an amended preliminary name declaration adding a distinctive element and re-file through the REQ online portal, which constitutes a new reservation without an administrative appeal fee; (2) request free reconsideration by the Registraire, attaching the refusal letter, a fresh name-search report, any trademark registrations, and an explanatory memorandum on French-language compliance; (3) if the Registraire maintains the refusal, contest the decision before the civil chamber of the Court of Quebec within 60 days of written notification of the second decision, filing an originating application signed by a Quebec-licensed lawyer, pursuant to the general administrative remedies under the Legal Publicity Act and the Code of Civil Procedure, CQLR c C-25.01; and (4) concurrently obtain a formal clearance opinion from the Office québécois de la langue française on the French version of the proposed name to prevent recurring language-based refusals.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not accepted as a statutory registered office. The REQ requires the declaration of registration to state the full civic address of the partnership's head office ('établissement principal') in Quebec where books and records are kept and legal documents may be served. Mail-forwarding virtual offices, bare co-working lounge addresses, or PO boxes do not satisfy the Legal Publicity Act standard. A physical office at the premises of a Quebec law firm or licensed corporate agent, with a dedicated unit number and staffed presence, is permissible and is the market-standard arrangement for a non-resident-owned ISIC 6311 voice streaming app company.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 12% aggregate probability of an unannounced on-site verification by REQ or Revenu Québec within the first 24 months for a fully digital app company using a registered-agent office; the probability increases to roughly 18% if the registered office is only an unstaffed address. FINTRAC examination risk is nominal provided the entity does not register as a money services business; a documented commercial substance file (local commercial office arrangement, local management contact, Quebec bank account, and Quebec-hosted records) materially reduces inspection and tax-treaty substance challenges.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preliminary name clearance (attestation de recherche de nom) at the Registraire d'entreprise du Québec
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the Regulation respecting the fees exigible by the Registraire des entreprises (approximately C$18-C$38 depending on document volume)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory registration (immatriculation) of the limited partnership 'société en commandite' under the Legal Publicity Act
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed statutory tariff of C$77 for enterprise registration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the French-language limited partnership agreement (contrat de société en commandite) and ancillary partner consent resolutions by a Quebec notary or licensed law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Chambre des notaires du Québec / licensed Quebec law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market flat fee for LP formation with bilingual support (C$1,200-C$1,500)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT KYC onboarding file: UBO piercing, 25% threshold verification, PEP and sanctions screening, adverse-media checks, and source-of-funds review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: FINTRAC-regulated Quebec formation agent / law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced corporate client file (C$450-C$550)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille and/or consular legalization of foreign partner identity documents and corporate certificates, with certified French/English translation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Global Affairs Canada, foreign competent authorities, Quebec certified translator, and notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document statutory consular and apostille fees plus prevailing certified-translation tariff (C$220-C$280 for a standard 4-document bundle)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First-year Quebec registered office services (physical commercial address in Montreal, service-of-process handling, and REQ correspondence management)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Quebec registered agent / law firm in Montreal
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for commercial registered-office services (C$400-C$600 per year)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec, arts. 2236–2261 (limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, ss. 1–33 and 74–80; Regulation respecting the fees payable under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, r. 1; Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11, s. 2.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar), an agency of the Ministry of Finance and authorized by the Inspector General of Financial Institutions.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Declaration of Registration) filed in the Registre des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Register).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed by Quebec law for a limited partnership. Contributions are determined by the partnership agreement and may be deferred; no escrow account or capital deposit rule applies. The Declaration of Registration must identify the general partner and state a domicile in Quebec for the enterprise.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the Corporation, acting as general partner of the Limited Partnership, hereby adopts the Limited Partnership Agreement in the form presented and approves the subscription of partnership interests, contributions being deferred per the agreement, there being no statutory minimum paid-in capital. RESOLVED FURTHER: That the registered office be established at [address], Quebec, and that the Secretary execute and file the Declaration of Registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. RESOLVED FURTHER: That [Name] be appointed Chief Manager and signing officer for banking, tax, and commercial matters, with authority to execute all ancillary documents. RESOLVED FINALLY: That all lawful acts performed prior to adoption are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Reservation with the Quebec Enterprise Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online portal, www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a prior name availability search in the Registre des entreprises du Québec and, if federal trademark or extra-provincial protection is desired, the NUANS database. Submit an online name-reservation request through the REQ 'Mon entreprise' portal using a REQ account or agent credentials; select the entity type 'Société en commandite (limited partnership)'. The reserved name is valid for 60 days and renewable; the name must include an element evoking a limited partnership (e.g., 'S.E.C.' or 'Limited Partnership') and, if used in Quebec, the French-language form must be declared unless an exemption under the Charter of the French Language applies.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form (REQ Form N-1 or online equivalent)
Power of attorney and identification of the mandatary (if filing through an agent)
French-name exemption request with supporting documents (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusion or non-compliance, reserve a revised name online immediately; alternatively, request a formal review by the REQ within 30 days under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, s. 27, attaching evidence of distinctiveness and prior use.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement and General Partner Adjudication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internal legal act — not filed with any government registry; kept with the LP's records at its Quebec domicile.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute (by private deed or notarial act) a Quebec-governed limited partnership agreement that clearly identifies the general partner (a corporation or natural person with unlimited liability) and the limited partners, the contribution terms, profit and loss allocation, management powers, withdrawal and dissolution provisions. If the general partner is a corporation, ensure its board adopts the first resolution approving the LP and that the corporation itself is registered at the REQ. The agreement remains confidential and is not part of the public register.
required_dossiers: Limited partnership agreement (original and duplicate copies)
Certified copy of the general partner's board resolution
Subscription schedule and capital contribution commitments
Identification documents (passport, driver's licence) for natural-person partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any defect by a written unanimous-partner resolution or by executing an amending agreement; if the agreement is ambiguous, obtain a declaration of intention signed by all partners. Legalized notarial execution may be sought to pre-empt banking and tax authentication disputes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Declaration of Registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — online filing service (secure electronic signature with a partner certificate or via the REQ 'Dématérialisation' channel).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online Declaration of Registration for a limited partnership: enter the reserved name, the exact LP classification ('société en commandite'), the domicile address in Quebec, the corporate or natural-person general partner's identifier (NEQ if registered), the limited partners' identification (or the statutory exemption if more than six and not required), the date of formation, and the main activity declared under the NAICS 2022 code 519130 (Other Internet Publishing and Broadcasting and Web Search Portals — interactive voice streaming). File the declaration electronically; the REQ charges approximately CAD 40 (USD 30) at current exchange rates. The LP acquires juridical personality only upon issuance of the attestation of registration, so filing must precede any contract or bank-account opening.
required_dossiers: Valid name reservation receipt (step 1)
Partners' legal name, domicile, date of birth (natural persons) or legal form and NEQ (juridical persons)
Proof of Quebec domicile (lease, utility bill, or notarial attestation)
Declaration of the general partner's mandate and full liability
NAICS 519130 activity declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ issues a notice of refusal or incompleteness, remedy by filing a corrective declaration within 30 days of the notice; if the deadline is missed, refile a new declaration with a fresh fee. A dispute over the refusal may be brought before the Court of Québec (Civil Division) within 60 days, or a request for an official review may be filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of NEQ and Attestation, Ongoing Registry Maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (registry services desk).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon acceptance, the REQ issues the enterprise's unique identification number (NEQ) and an attestation of registration. Verify that all registered data match the LP agreement and immediately correct any discrepancy. Thereafter, file any modification (change of partners, change of domicile, change of general partner) within 30 days of the change, and file the annual updating declaration between the anniversary date and December 31 each year. The LP must also display its name and NEQ on all correspondence and signage in accordance with Quebec law.
required_dossiers: Attestation of registration issued by the REQ
Copy of the filed Declaration of Registration (stamped or electronic)
Internal log of the NEQ and registry access credentials
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Apply to the REQ for rectification of any inaccurate disclosure under articles 25–28 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; in case of delay, submit an administrative follow-up form, and if refused, seek judicial correction in the Court of Québec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax Registration (CRA and Revenu Québec)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online portal; Revenu Québec — 'Mon dossier d'entreprise' portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the LP with the CRA for a nine-digit federal Business Number (BN) and, if applicable, the GST/HST account (the app's revenue from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing is taxable supply; the LP should evaluate the deemed-vendor rules for marketplace facilitators). Concurrently, register with Revenu Québec for the QST account under the Act respecting the Québec sales tax (CQLR c T-0.1), for employer health contribution and CNESST registration if employees are hired, and for the QST on digital services to Quebec consumers. Provide the NEQ and attestation, the LP agreement, and banking details; accept electronic notices and mandate an authorized representative. Registration should be completed immediately after step 3 to avoid assessment exposure on launch.
required_dossiers: NEQ attestation (step 4)
Limited partnership agreement
Corporate general partner's resolutions and certificate
Bank account details (Canadian financial institution)
Projected revenue estimates and expected effective date of taxable supply
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed, file under the CRA/Revenu Québec Voluntary Disclosures Program (VDP) to waive penalties; if the authorities levy penalties, request taxpayer relief under CRA s. 220 and Revenu Québec s. 27.1, demonstrating reasonable diligence and the absence of wilful default.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Sectoral Screening — Online Communications and Platform Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission (CRTC) — Online Streaming Act implementation (if applicable); otherwise internal compliance officer; app distribution governed by Apple App Store and Google Play developer agreements.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare a legal memorandum assessing whether the interactive voice-streaming social app constitutes an 'online communications service' (OCS) under the Online Streaming Act (S.C. 2023, c. 8) or merely a real-time 'social audio' service exempt from Part II of the Broadcasting Act. For a typical two-way interactive chatroom platform that is not a linear audio service, no CRTC registration or licence is expected; however, if the service later offers a catalogue of recorded or broadcast-like content, file a registration declaration with the CRTC as prescribed in the OCS registration regulations. Also verify that no telecommunications carrier licence (Telecom Act) is required, as the app rides on underlying third-party IP networks. Confirm compliance with PIPEDA for personal information and the Quebec Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector (CQLR c P-39.1).
required_dossiers: Legal assessment memo (OCS threshold analysis)
App privacy policy and terms of service
Data-management and consent framework
Apple/Google developer account certificates
Compliance attestation under Charter of the French Language for in-app interfaces
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRTC issues a notice requiring OCS registration, file within the prescribed deadline without prejudice and, if the service does not meet the definition, submit an explanatory submission and request an exemption order; any disputed CRTC determination may be appealed to the Federal Court of Appeal under the Broadcasting Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for the digital activity; for any physical administrative office the local municipality is the competent authority for a business licence (permis d'exploitation). At the provincial level, the Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MEIE) maintains informational programs but issues no licence for application-software operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required for the voice-streaming application itself. Distribution is governed by the Apple App Store and Google Play Store developer agreements (commercial contracts, not governmental licences). If the LP leases premises in Quebec, the municipal business permit and the REQ identification certificate must be obtained, and the enterprise name displayed in accordance with the Charter of the French Language.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category: Exempt — no industrial project or contaminant-emitting activity; purely digital/administrative operation. No certificate of authorization is required under the Environment Quality Act, CQLR c Q-2, ss. 22 and 31.1, because the activity is not listed in Schedule I or II of the Regulation respecting the environmental impact assessment, CQLR c Q-2, r. 1.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC, or hazardous-waste discharge generated by the platform. Leased office premises must comply with municipal sewer and water by-laws; disposal of defective IT equipment is subject to the Residual Hazardous Waste Regulation, CQLR c Q-2, r. 35. Any third-party cloud/data-center infrastructure is operated by the provider under ISO 14001 and applicable Canadian environmental law; no direct LP compliance is triggered.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable to the virtual service. For a leased Quebec office: (i) obtain from the landlord or the municipal fire-prevention department a certificate of fire-safety compliance under the Building Act (CQLR c B-1.1) and the Quebec Construction Code; (ii) register the establishment with the CNESST and comply with the Act respecting occupational health and safety (CQLR c S-2.1), including a workplace first-aid kit, emergency evacuation plan, and electrical-equipment inspection as applicable; (iii) no structural load or special physical clearance is required for a standard administrative occupancy.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Federal income and GST/HST tax administration; Revenu Quebec (ARQ) - Quebec Sales Tax (QST), Quebec income tax and payroll obligations. Portals: CRA My Business Account and Revenu Quebec CLIC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Quebec limited partnership (LP) must first file a declaration of registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ), obtaining a Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ). It must then obtain a CRA Business Number (BN) by filing Form RC4601 or RC1 and register for GST/HST under section 240 of the Excise Tax Act, providing the partnership's legal name, address and Canadian or foreign identification. For QST, the LP must register with Revenu Quebec using Form LM-1 or via CLIC. Non-resident partners must identify themselves with their foreign tax identification numbers and may be subject to Canadian Part XIII withholding or section 116 clearance, but this does not alter the LP's registration obligation. Foreign entities acting through the LP must evidence their existence and beneficial ownership through certified constituent documents, power of attorney and Revenu Quebec/short-form registration proof.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box election exists under Canadian law. The LP is automatically fiscally transparent for income tax purposes, with income/loss allocated to partners. Available elections include: (i) election under Excise Tax Act s. 156 for GST/HST grouping of closely related registrants, if applicable; (ii) specified investment flow-through (SIFT) trust/partnership election under ITA s. 122.1 for publicly traded or certain listed LPs; (iii) Quebec QST registration and filing elections with Revenu Quebec, including joint election for non-resident registrants using an agent or mandatary.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) and Quebec Sales Tax (QST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 (for both GST/HST and QST; the small-supplier threshold is measured on worldwide taxable supplies by the partnership and mandatory registration applies once taxable supplies exceed C$30,000 in any particular calendar quarter or in the preceding four calendar quarters, or whenever the LP makes taxable supplies in Canada while carrying on business in Canada and no small-supplier relief is available)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, digital stamping or government pre-approval of individual invoices is currently mandated by CRA or Revenu Quebec for GST/HST/QST. Invoices must contain prescribed data required by s. 169 of the Excise Tax Act and the Quebec Taxation Act, including supplier registration number, date of invoice, vendor and purchaser names, tax rates and amounts. E-invoices are permitted if in an accessible electronic format that is tamper-evident and retains a complete audit trail.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported by the LP may be zero-rated under s. 23 of the Excise Tax Act if exported in accordance with the customs laws and the LP retains proof of export. Services supplied to a non-resident, including voice streaming, interactive audio and digital platform services, are zero-rated under s. 23(2) where the service is supplied to a non-resident and the service is not considered to be performed in Canada (i.e., the subscription or usage is delivered and enjoyed outside Canada). The LP must use customer location indicators such as billing address, IP geolocation and identifiable foreign network use to evidence non-resident supply. Quebec QST zero-rating for exports and external services follows analogous rules in the Quebec Taxation Act. The zero-rating criterion is not satisfied where the underlying service is rendered to Canadian users through the app, even if billing is made by an offshore payment provider.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian Customs Export Declaration (CBSA electronic export declaration or prescribed customs form)
Bill of Lading / air waybill / electronic transport evidence

Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit confirmation showing receipt of foreign-sourced payment in Canadian currency; for digital/voice streaming services, supplementary contract, IP-geolocation report and platform payout statements
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA and Revenu Quebec may reassess to disallow zero-rating, re-characterize the supply as taxable, assess unremitted GST/HST and QST, plus interest and penalties. Fraudulent or gross-negligent export zero-rating claims are subject to penalties under s. 285 of the Excise Tax Act (25% of the amount improperly claimed or refunded) and s. 281.1 (up to 200% of the evaded tax for evasion). Revenu Quebec may apply an additional penalty of up to 50% for false statements under the Taxation Act, and the normal four-year reassessment period is extended indefinitely in cases of misrepresentation or fraud. General partners may become personally liable where the partnership's claim is made for a sham or abusive transaction.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); prudential oversight of federally chartered banks by Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); anti-money laundering supervision by FINTRAC; sanctions administration by Global Affairs Canada and the Minister of Finance
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a free-floating currency under a liberalized capital and current account regime. The Canadian dollar is fully convertible for residents and non-residents; there are no general exchange control laws requiring central bank approval for capital inflows, dividend remittances, or repatriation. Profit remittance from a Quebec Limited Partnership is structurally treated as a distribution to partners, not a dividend, so no Quebec dividend withholding tax applies to non-resident partners if properly structured; however, the Canada Revenue Agency may apply withholding under Part XIII for payments that in substance are interest, rent, royalties, or management fees. Investor and trade compliance triggers include the Investment Canada Act for non-resident control acquisitions, the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) reporting, Canada’s Beneficial Ownership Transparency regime, and the sanctions screening obligations under the United Nations Act and the Special Economic Measures Act. Practical conversion friction is limited to bank FX spreads, correspondent bank compliance, and FINTRAC cross-border wire reporting thresholds (C$10,000 or any designated amount).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement, no stipulated timeline for converting foreign currency received into Canadian dollars, and no mandatory conversion ratio. In-app marketplace proceeds denominated in USD, EUR, or other foreign currencies may be retained, swept, or converted at the taxpayer’s discretion, subject to the Quebec IT Partnership’s obligation to report income in Canadian dollars under applicable GAAP/tax rules and to substantiate foreign currency transactions for CRA audit purposes. High-value cross-border transfers above CAD 10,000 must be monitored and reported to FINTRAC where required.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operating Account - Canadian Dollar Base Currency with USD sub-account; dedicated Capital Contribution Clearing Account
Dual Currency Operating and Settlement Account; segregated Escrow/Trust Account for partner capital
Global Business Operating Account; non-resident partner capital account with zero-minimum balance arrangement
Enterprise Operating Account and Trade Settlement Sub-Account; USD sweep facility
Operating plus Payment Gateway Concentration Account; LC collateral account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility subject to strict structure. Canada does not use the EU EMI licence concept; Canadian regulated equivalents are MSBs registered with FINTRAC and provincially regulated in Quebec, or federally regulated banks chartered by OSFI. An offshore EMI with no Canadian MSB registration may lawfully provide payment processing to the Quebec LP, but it cannot legally hold, transmit, or settle customer funds in Canada without a registrable money-services business licence. For treasury operations, an offshore EMI used only as a vendor settlement rail for app-store payouts is viable only where the EMI is not the primary custody account, is not used to collect from Canadian consumers, and does not create a PEP/sanctions concentration risk. The LP should require an internationally domiciled EMI with OSFI or FINTRAC equivalence, segregated client accounts, and full FATF membership in its home jurisdiction; the recommended reserve account remains a tier-1 Canadian bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A mandatory physical appearance at a Montreal or Quebec City branch is the general baseline for first-time corporate account openings at major Canadian banks, especially for limited partnerships with non-resident partners and a pre-revenue app business. Remote onboarding is available under PCMLTFA-compliant customer identification measures (e.g., video identification plus certified passport copies, Canadian corporate registry extracts, notarized partnership deeds), but Canadian banks in practice require the general partner’s Canadian resident representative or a director/authorized signatory to complete an in-person or documented video interview. Financial crime risk personnel may require a physical bank visit at a designated branch for the final meeting if any beneficial owner, jurisdiction, or industry trigger elevates the risk profile above standard. Keeping at least one Canadian resident general partner signatory materially increases onboarding success and avoids Frustrated Offshore Client rules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Quebec Limited Partnership with a non-resident general partner and opaque beneficial ownership chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Original notarized declaration of partnership; (2) Registraire des entreprises du Québec certificate of registration; (3) complete register of beneficial owners showing natural-person partners, control percentages, and source of capital; (4) Canadian tax legal opinion confirming LP pass-through classification and the absence of corporate nominee ownership; (5) sanctions and politically exposed persons questionnaires for every partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pre-revenue mobile voice streaming business with high app-store transaction volume and no audited financials
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Board-approved 24-month business plan and liquidity model; (2) contractual evidence of Apple App Store and Google Play developer agreements; (3) pro-forma revenue recognition policy and expected payout schedule; (4) principal shareholder bank reference and source-of-funds declaration; (5) certified booking or initial capital ledger entries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Risk of use for unlicensed money transmission or payments intermediation through in-app virtual currencies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Legal opinion that the LP is not carrying on money services business because app-store payment rails are acting as merchant-of-record; (2) FINTRAC MSB registration exemption analysis; (3) terms of service and end-user licences disclaiming digital-asset storage; (4) chargeback and refund control policy; (5) third-party compliance audit of the payment routing logic.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border flow from high-risk jurisdictions through customer base made possible by global app distribution
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Country blocklist configured at the application and payment processor level; (2) sanctions screening policy under Global Affairs Canada Consolidated List; (3) transaction monitoring policy and threshold-based escalation matrix; (4) IP-geolocation and VPN-detection controls; (5) annual independent PCMLTFA compliance review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Quebec-specific language and consumer protection exposure creating an operational red flag for banking underwriters
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Compliance certification for Quebec’s Charter of the French Language covering app UI, billing, and customer contracts; (2) Quebec Consumer Protection Act analysis; (3) privacy impact assessment under Quebec Law 25; (4) app-store jurisdiction configuration; (5) sample EULA and refund policy in French and English.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from non-resident partners should be routed by SWIFT MT103 or Fedwire-style correspondent transfer to a dedicated Capital Contribution Clearing Account at a tier-1 Canadian bank. The CAD amount must be received as a clean corporate bank-to-bank credit, not as a consumer-style payment, and the payment message should include the LP’s Quebec registry number, the partner legal entity name, and the narrative 'Unrestricted Partner Capital Contribution.' The bank will require an underlying partnership capital call notice, evidence of partner identity, and confirmation that the contribution is not a loan. Where the contribution exceeds CAD 10,000, the bank must report the transaction to FINTRAC under cross-border funds transfer rules; where the contributing partner is resident in a FATF-listed high-risk jurisdiction, enhanced source-of-funds documentation, a sanctions sweep, and potentially an OSFI reporting obligation apply. The account should never be used for customer settlements or operational revenue; once the contribution is received, the LP’s general partner should transfer the cleared funds to the primary Operating Account using an internal journal entry or separate MT103, preserving a clean capital trace for the Quebec tax filings and the CRA foreign-sourced contribution schedule.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound treasury disbursements for trade settlement should use two primary rails: (1) standard corporate wire via SWIFT MT103 for habitual supplier payments, licensing fees, and marketing disbursements; and (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (documentary credits) issued by the Canadian bank or opened through a correspondent bank for substantial infrastructure procurements where the counterparty requires payment against shipping or delivery documents. For app-store payouts and recurring SaaS or CDN vendor payments, automated clearing (ACH/Electronic Funds Transfer in Canada plus SWIFT for USD/EUR vendors) is preferred over wire to reduce cost. All outbound payments must include correct purpose details, CRA source document references, and transfer pricing support where the payee is a related foreign entity. If applicable under Regulations, Part XII.2 tax on dividends or Part XIII withholding applies to certain cross-border payments; therefore the treasury policy must preclear any interest, royalty, management fee, or consulting fee through a withholding tax opinion before disbursement. Payment stop-payment, fraud controls, and dual-authorisation signatory rules must be embedded in the online banking platform for every outbound transfer above the bank’s standard threshold.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR) traded under ISDA/CSA master agreement with a Canadian Schedule I bank
FX Swaps and Cross-Currency Swaps to hedge operational cash-flow exposure arising from USD-denominated app-store receivables
Over-the-counter vanilla CAD FX options (calls and puts) with physical delivery or cash settlement

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) in permitted regional currencies where the counterparty confirms the NDF is used for hedge-only commercial exposure and no local exchange control prohibition exists in the underlying currency jurisdiction
Bank-offered FX forward packages embedded in dual-currency operating accounts provided the hedging instrument is clearly segregated from speculative positions
Interest rate cross-currency basis swaps combined with a Canadian dollar funding facility where the hedge is solely for the contracted future trade settlements
In the event that counterparty credit is challenged, a collateralised forward overlay using tri-party collateral in the form of Canadian Treasury Bills is permissible

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of sole proprietorships, partnerships and legal persons (Quebec)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of the declaration made in the Registraire des entreprises (i.e., original registration anniversary)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fees and, if the declaration remains unfiled for two consecutive years, the registraire may issue a notice of dissolution/strike-off; administrative penalties may be imposed under the Legal Publicity Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return and T5013 slips
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the partnership fiscal period end (for a December 31 year-end, the T5013 return is due by May 31); partner copies must be provided by March 31 or corresponding third-month rule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalties under the Income Tax Act (e.g., $25/day for the return up to a statutory maximum), late-slip penalties per partner, interest on any unpaid balance, and possible criminal prosecution for repeated omissions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Relevé de renseignements RL-15 (Partnership information) and applicable provincial return to Revenu Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually; RL-15 slips must be filed with Revenu Québec and provided to partners no later than the last day of February following the calendar year-end (or the last day of the third month after the fiscal period end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Provincial penalties per late or missing RL-15 slip, interest on unreported amounts, and administrative monetary penalties for continued non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory entity-level audit is imposed on a Quebec limited partnership solely by reason of size or revenue under the Taxation Act. A mandatory independent audit is required by contract or by partnership agreement when the LP has institutional investors or is a reporting issuer, or when CRA/Revenu Québec serves a demand for audited financial statements under a formal production-of-records requirement. Corporate general partners becoming subject to Quebec Business Corporations Act audit thresholds may require consolidated audited financials.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) or International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS). ASPE is the default for private partnerships; IFRS is required if the LP is a publicly accountable entity or if a partner is subject to securities legislation and consolidates the LP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Québec does not maintain a separate beneficial-ownership register for limited partnerships. The registered annual declaration must identify all general partners; limited partners' names and contributions are recorded in the partnership agreement and in the partnership's internal registers but are not necessarily public if the declaration states only general partners. The general partner must review and confirm the continued accuracy of the register of limited partners and any transfers, and must file amending declarations within the prescribed delay after any change of partner. For AML purposes, the LP's registered agent or financial service provider will require an annual UBO questionnaire confirming the beneficial owners of each partner.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of General Partners and Capital Contributions
Register of Limited Partners and Transferable Partnership Interests
Minute Book of Partnership Resolutions and General Partner Decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - 600 per year for a commercial registered office and annual declaration service in Quebec
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - 8,500 for a certified independent audit of a medium-risk technology/LP entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% (combined federal 15% + Quebec 11.5% general corporate rate) for tax-paying corporate partners; the Limited Partnership itself is fiscally transparent and does not pay corporate income tax
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal small business deduction reduces the federal rate to 9% on the first C$500,000 of active business income for Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs); Quebec offers a preferential reduced provincial rate for eligible SMEs (as low as 4%) on the first C$500,000; digital voice streaming and app revenue normally qualifies for these rates if carried on in Canada through a CCPC partner

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T5013 Partnership Information Return filed via CRA My Business Account or certified tax preparation software
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: March 31 of the year following a calendar fiscal year-end; otherwise the 15th day of the third month after the partnership fiscal period-end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business revenue from all Canadian and foreign sources
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross proceeds from in-app subscriptions, voice-streaming tokens, and virtual gifts after deduction of Apple/Google platform commissions; allocate to partners according to the partnership agreement

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible business expenses (salaries, infrastructure, advertising, platform fees)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenses incurred for the Canadian partnership business; related-party charges must comply with s. 247 transfer pricing rules

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income (loss) for the partnership's Canada-based activity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This amount is allocated to each partner; a non-resident partner's share is subject to Canadian Part I tax on a net basis and may require quarterly instalments

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, residency, TIN, and classification of each partner
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide a valid certificate of residence from the partner's tax authority to support treaty relief; ensure allocation percentages reconcile with the partnership agreement

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under ITA s. 162(5): C$25 per day, maximum C$2,500 (partnerships with more than 5 partners) or maximum C$500 (5 or fewer partners); false statements attract a 50% gross negligence penalty on the understated tax

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quebec: CO-17 Déclaration de renseignements des sociétés de personnes filed via Revenu Québec's clicSÉQUR Affaires
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same as the federal T5013: March 31 for a calendar fiscal year-end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income from a business carried on in Quebec
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile with federal Line 1; allocate to partners using the same allocation used for T5013
State each non-resident partner's share separated; note whether tax was withheld or a net-basis Part I election was made

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Revenu Québec penalty under the Taxation Act (RLRQ c. I-3): C$25 per day up to C$2,500 for late filing, plus interest on unpaid Quebec instalments

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII for dividends paid by a Canadian corporation to non-resident shareholders; however, an LP is fiscally transparent and its profit distribution to partners is not a dividend — a non-resident partner is taxed under Part I on allocated business income at progressive rates, with no Part XIII withholding on the distribution itself
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident partner claiming a DTA benefit must deliver a current certificate of residence from the treaty jurisdiction to the Canadian partnership before the T5013 is filed or before any Part XIII withholding applies; for Part XIII items, the withholding agent applies the treaty rate after receiving CRA Form NR301 or an equivalent ERP; if excess tax was withheld, the non-resident submits Form NR7-R to claim a refund; for a flow-through LP, a treaty relief claim is documented in the non-resident partner's T1/NR4 tax return and supported by the partnership's allocation schedule
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate on royalties and non-arm's-length interest is 25%; arm's-length interest is exempt under ITA s. 212(3)(b) (0%); Canada–US treaty reduces royalties to 10% (0% for copyright/computer software in certain cases) and portfolio interest to 0%; Canada–UK treaty commonly 10% on royalties and 10% on interest

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: C$250,000 for a single cross-border non-arm's-length transaction and C$1,000,000 for the aggregate annual value of all such transactions with a related party; Country-by-Country reporting is triggered for groups with consolidated revenue above C$750 million
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not maintain formal ESR, but the s. 245 General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and the OECD MLI Principal Purpose Test (PPT) deny treaty benefits and re-characterize transactions that lack economic substance; a Canadian LP created solely to route passive royalties or in-app revenue to a low-tax affilate without real employees, premises, or business decisions is presumed to be an artificial conduit and may be reassessed with penalties

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting gross revenue from Apple IAP/Google Play Billing or misallocating partnership income among partners to avoid Canadian and Quebec tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under ITA s. 163(2), gross negligence penalty of 50% of understated tax; under ITA s. 239(1), imprisonment up to 5 years for tax evasion; fines up to 200% of the evaded tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a corporate general partner may be jointly and severally liable under ITA s. 160; civil restitution, fraud charges, travel ban, and incarceration for up to 5 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying royalties, interest, management fees, or distributions of a taxable character to non-resident partners without withholding the statutory 25% or an applicable treaty-reduced rate
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under ITA s. 227(8), penalty of 10% of the amount not withheld and remitted, plus interest and arrears; failure to file an information return can add C$25/day penalties up to C$2,500
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the general partner are personally liable under ITA s. 227.1 for the unremitted withholding, plus interest, penalties and civil suit; repeated violations can trigger travel restrictions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting intercompany payments to a foreign affiliate for limited functionality (e.g., IP licensing) without contemporaneous TP study, or relying on a CUP that is not comparably adjusted
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under ITA s. 247(3), a penalty of 10% of the net transfer-pricing adjustment if the correction exceeds the lesser of C$2,000,000 and 10% of gross revenue; the CRA may adjust to arm's-length terms and deny deduction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not automatically liable for TP penalties, but can become liable under s. 227.1 if the adjustment leads to unremitted withholding; gross negligence could trigger s. 163(2) and personal criminal exposure for false documentation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the voice streaming app with a Medium-Risk rating and processing in-app payments without an AML risk assessment, transaction monitoring, or reporting suspicious transactions to FINTRAC
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, administrative monetary penalties up to C$500,000 per violation for a partnership; criminal charge under Criminal Code s. 462.31 for laundering proceeds — imprisonment up to 10 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers of the general partner may receive personal fines up to C$1,000,000, imprisonment up to 10 years, asset freezes and travel bans; civil suits for restitution are common where the LP is used as a conduit

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Quebec LP exclusively to invoice Canadian app revenue to a no-tax affiliate in a different jurisdiction, with no personnel, servers, or decision-making in Canada
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR allows the CRA to disregard the arrangement and reallocate income to the Canadian entity; interest and penalties accrue on the reassessed tax, and the principal purpose test under the MLI may deny treaty protection entirely
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held civilly liable for losses caused by reckless structuring, receive a ban on serving as officers, and face criminal charges for counselling tax evasion; extradition possible under mutual legal assistance treaties
